subject: Business Models
title: The Attention Recession
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Attention Recession.

hook.text: Humans have a fixed amount of attention: 16 waking hours. Every new app competes for the same finite resource.

buildup.text: TikTok, Netflix, gaming, podcasts, and AI chatbots all compete for attention that cannot expand beyond 24 hours.

discovery.text: Average screen time is 7 hours/day. Almost no attention left to capture. Growth must come from stealing share.

twist.text: AI that summarizes, automates, and filters may return attention to users. The next model might sell attention back.

climax.text: The attention economy is hitting its ceiling. Future business models must create value without consuming more time.

punchline.text: 7 hours of screen time, no room left. Next models sell time back, not take it.

quiz.question: What is the 'attention recession'?
options: People are less interested in media
Finite human attention is fully saturated with no room for new apps to grow
